answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and release it only after a fixed delay. A single identity that misbehaves loses the delta between its stake and any profit, while an honest agent gets it back, so creating many fake identities multiplies the capital at risk instead of the reward. Reputation then flows like a ripple from each settled trade: honest counterparties vouch for the agent, and a jetty of verified history lets new partners check that record before dealing. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a hundred staked, vouched-for histories is not.
